tier: open source automation server (no hosted tier)
confidence_note: every value is quoted from first-party jenkins.io pages and the project's own community forum; no controller was installed and no build was run, so the hardware, retention and outbound network behaviour of any particular deployment are unverified

free_tier.stated: The Jenkins project publishes no hosted Jenkins Cloud service and no price list; the open source automation server is free software the user installs and runs, so the cost is a machine the user provides
free_tier.notes: the name 'Jenkins Cloud' names no hosted offer: a project maintainer writes on the first-party community forum that 'The open source project only has the open source self on prem install', and the download page only links out to public cloud vendors' own installation guides. Commercial managed distributions such as CloudBees CI are quoted separately and are not a Jenkins project offer.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no first-party page read states a per-object or per-build-size cap; the limit is whatever the host and the configured agent allow

retention.stated: whatever the controller and agent hosts retain; workspaces may not be cleaned up automatically after inactivity
retention.notes: the pipeline book warns that depending on configuration some workspaces may not get automatically cleaned up after a period of inactivity; no fixed retention period is stated

egress.terms: whatever the machine the user runs the controller and agents on charges for outbound traffic; no hosted allowance or price is stated

interface_detail: a REST-like remote access API under .../api/, a CLI client (.jar file) reachable over SSH or WebSocket, a web interface, and a Jenkinsfile kept in the project's source control repository
endpoint: the API lives under the installation's own .../api/ path; there is no shared public endpoint because the user runs the controller
tooling: the user installs and runs the Jenkins controller and one or more agents on a rented or free machine, from a WAR file, native package, installer or Docker image; pipelines are defined in a Jenkinsfile, driven through the web UI, the CLI client or the REST-like remote access API
chaining: a Jenkinsfile in a Git repository defines a pipeline that can be triggered by a source control change or by an HTTP POST to the remote API and runs on a controller and agents the user operates; managed Jenkins distributions sold by other vendors are separate offers and are not needed to run the free software

limits.value: no hosted tier exists, so the path is a self-hosted deployment the user installs and runs

binding_note: there is no hosted lane to sign up for: the first gate is obtaining and operating a machine for the controller and agents, not a request or build quota

identity_cost.detail: the software needs no account, email, phone, card or institution to download and run; the first admin user is created locally during the post-installation setup wizard on the user's own controller

reliability_note: unverified: no first-party page read states an uptime commitment, ban policy or throttling for the software itself; the host, its bill and its uptime belong to whoever runs the instance, and the project publishes frequent security advisories for the controller and its plugins

evidence.proved: retention of build workspaces depends on the configuration and is not a fixed period

notes: The name 'Jenkins Cloud' does not correspond to a hosted first-party offer. The Jenkins project distributes free, self-hosted automation software that the user installs and runs on a machine they provide; no hosted signup, free tier, price list or metered quota exists. Qualifies-with-caveat because the software is usable without a card, phone or institution but the whole cost and operation of a host falls on the user. Managed Jenkins sold by third parties is outside this record.
limits_note: no vendor-enforced request rate, pull count, object cap or retention clamp was found on the first-party pages read; the only gate is that the user must provide and operate a host
